start: Look... something is shining out there on the horizon. Or we could climb that tall dune and see everything. Where should we go?
water-glint: It keeps shimmering. Could it be water? Or is the desert playing tricks on us? Help me decide.
oasis: Water... it's real. Should I touch it? Or follow those little tracks in the mud? Someone else has been here.
pool-glow: It glows where I touch it. Look at the reflection... or should I step right in? What do you feel?
star-reflection: Stars, in the middle of the day. One is falling. Should we follow it? Or fill up and keep walking?
pool-steps: There are steps under the water, going down to a soft glow. Down into the dark, or back to the light?
crystal-cave: The crystals are humming. That big one is calling me... but I feel a cool breeze too. Which way?
crystal-hum: It answered me. Should I take a little piece of its light with me? Or follow the rings outside?
shard-lantern: Now we have our own light. Daylight is that way... but someone carved this tunnel. Should we explore it?
tunnel-hall: Lanterns, floating everywhere. Should I set one free? Or walk to the end of the hall and see what waits there?
cave-exit: The sun again, warmer now. The old ruins are close... or we could walk until the stars come out.
fox-meet: Oh... hello, little one. A fox made of metal, like me. Should we walk together? Or see where it runs?
fox-joins: I think it wants to show us something. Should we let it lead? Or climb the big dune together?
fox-leads: It brought us to the ruins. Should we search them? Or follow it through that carved door?
dune-top: From up here I can see ruins below... and something huge is moving under the sand. What should we do?
sand-whale: A whale made of sand... it's beautiful. Should I climb on and ride it? Or let it swim away?
whale-ride: We're sailing through the dunes. It's starting to dive... hold on? Or jump off at the ruins?
whale-dive: It left me by a crack in the sand. There's a glow deep inside. Should I go deeper? Or climb back out?
ruins: These stones are older than me. There's a little niche there... and a carved door. Which one first?
parchment: A parchment... it feels warm, like it knows me. Should I unroll it? Or read these runes out loud?
map-glow: A map made of light. That line is pointing somewhere. Should we follow it? Or keep it for later?
golden-path: The light is leading us to a gate. Should we walk up to it? Or keep walking until night falls?
sand-stairs: The sand is building stairs... into the sky. Should I climb them? Or keep my feet on the ground?
sky-island: An island in the clouds. I could ride a cloud back down... or take the stairs. What do you think?
stairs-down: Back on the sand. The ruins are still there... or the open dunes. Where to now?
cloud-glide: The cloud brought us to a stone gate. Should we go up to it? Or keep wandering the dunes?
ancient-door: A hall full of floating lanterns. Should I let one fly? Or walk all the way to the end?
lanterns: They're rising into the evening sky. Walk under them until dark? Or follow where they drift?
hall-end: A gate standing all alone. The air inside moves like water. Should we step through? Or walk around it?
gate: This gate is humming. The air inside ripples like water. Step through with me? Or leave it be?
glass-desert: A desert made of glass... and two moons. Should we walk toward them? Or go back through the gate?
two-moons: It's so quiet here. Should we go back through the gate? Or follow that shooting star home?
back-through: Our dunes again. Should we head for the ruins? Or walk on until nightfall?
star-home: The star landed just ahead. Should we find where it fell? Or walk on and watch the night come?
mirage: A city, floating above the sand. Is it real? Should I walk into it? Or turn back to the dunes?
mirage-city: The mirage became real. That tallest tower touches the clouds. Climb it? Or follow the banners out?
tower-top: I can see the whole desert from here. A pink cloud is passing by... jump on? Or climb back down?
mirage-fade: The city is fading like a dream. The ruins are near... or we walk until night. You choose.
open-desert: Just us and the wind now. Should we go to the old ruins? Or keep walking until the stars come out?
night-falls: The stars are coming out. There's a campfire over there... or that bright star is calling. Which one?
campfire: A fire in the dark, and stars falling everywhere. Walk on until sunrise? Or chase one of them?
star-crater: A tiny star, resting in the sand. Should I pick it up? Or let it keep shining here?
dawn: A new day. That glint on the horizon again... or the tallest dune. Where do we begin this time?
walk: The desert is so wide... and so quiet. Should I keep walking on my own? Or would you like a little fox to come with me?
alone: Just me and the wind, then. I see palm trees to the left... and to the right, the sand is moving. Which way?
fox-comes: I see palm trees to the left... and to the right, the sand is moving. Which way should we go?
left-oasis: Water... it's real. Should I trail my hand in it? Or rest in the shade of the palms for a while?
right-ruins: These stones are older than me. There's a little niche there... and a carved door. Which one first?
focus: I am losing focus... I need to find myself. And the only way is to stop. Let me find a quiet spot, sit down, and just breathe.
stillness: There is so much information in the world. Scrolling, social media, streaming, the rush and pace of the cities. We need to slow down, little by little. For me, and I hope for you, it is about sitting down and closing your eyes. Just a couple of minutes each day brings me peace. I remembered this thanks to this journey with you, here in the desert.
alone-reaction: It's hard, sometimes, to be alone... but walking on my own a little longer feels good.
fox-reaction: It can be a fox... it can be anybody. But having somebody near you is the best feeling in the world.
oasis-reaction: We call it planet Earth, and out here in the desert it really feels that way. But it would be amazing to have a little bit of water... it's such an amazing element.
ruins-reaction: Ruins tell us about our past... and remind us that we all leave a mark. It starts to fade away, but the mark will still be there, long after we are gone.
